speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes, and how long they typically last? Do you have any awareness of your surroundings while they are occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have any history of fever, head trauma, or recent infections prior to the onset of these episodes? Do you notice any rhythmic jerking movements of the limbs during the grimacing, or is it purely facial and hand automatisms?

speaker: Doctor
text: No fever, head trauma, or recent infections. The movements are primarily facial grimacing and hand automatisms, without rhythmic jerking of the limbs. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the temporal lobe EEG findings and the aura of a strange taste, this is highly suggestive of focal impaired awareness seizures. Are there any other triggers you've noticed, such as sleep deprivation or stress, and does the patient have any family history of epilepsy?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the clinical presentation and EEG findings, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
